_notes: ⚠ THE REPLAY LEG IS BROKEN — issue 860, found by this capture. §8.3's alreadySubmitted is a SUCCESS the client treats identically to submitted, and it is what lets a client that lost the first response recover the documentNo. The session gate refuses the retry as SESSION_CLOSED first, and no other response on this contract carries a documentNo — so that order number is currently unrecoverable. `retryRefused` records that rather than the promise.

The mint itself is real and once-only holds in the DB: OrderNo := TransactionId under the filtered unique index UX_SdDocumentHeader_CLCN_OrderNo (786). What 860 blocks is the WIRE's ability to report it back on a retry.
There is no 'unknown' outcome. 133 ruled the reuse of 278's orchestration IN-PROCESS, not HTTP-to-self, which removes the in-flight gap that would produce one.

🚩 SUBMIT_UNAVAILABLE returns 503 but MUST carry the envelope — core/api.ts maps a bare status >= 500 to kind:'server' ('unexpected'), so an envelope-less 503 turns a routine retryable outcome into a crash on screen. That pairing is asserted code-by-code (including the 503) by CallCenterWebRefusalTableTests; it is not reproducible on demand here, which is why this fixture captures the two SUCCESS outcomes and leaves the two refusals to that table.
127's 12h sweeper would auto-void a transaction whose order was actually minted; 786's hosted reconciler + sweeper guard is what keeps this fixture honest.
